627-essays-of-travel.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. rst encountered my fellow-passengers on the Broomielaw in Glasgow. Thence we descended the Clyde in no familiar spirit, but looking askance on each other as on possible enemies. A few Scandinavians, who had already grown acquainted on the North Sea, were friendly and voluble over their long pipes; but among English speakers distance and suspicion reigned supreme.

His years are young, but his experience old;  His head unmellow’d, but his judgment ripe;  He is complete in feature and in mind,  With all good grace, to grace a gentleman.

arxiv-1902-10323.title: Quantifying Dissipation in Actomyosin Networks
arxiv-1902-10323.creator: Carlos Floyd, Garegin A. Papoian, Christopher Jarzynski
arxiv-1902-10323.description: Abstract Quantifying entropy production in various active matter phases will open new avenues for probing self-organization principles in these far-from-equilibrium systems. It has been hypothesized that the dissipation of free energy by active matter systems may be optimized to produce highly dissipative dynamical states, hence, leading to spontaneous emergence of more ordered states.

arxiv-2101-12235.title: Factorised 3d 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 orthosymplectic quivers
arxiv-2101-12235.creator: Mohammad Akhond, Federico Carta, Siddharth Dwivedi, Hirotaka Hayashi, Sung-Soo Kim, and Futoshi Yagi
arxiv-2101-12235.description: Abstract We study the moduli space of 3d 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 quiver gauge theories with unitary, orthogonal and symplectic gauge nodes, that fall into exceptional sequences. We find that both the Higgs and Coulomb branches of the moduli space factorise into decoupled sectors. Each decoupled sector is described by a single quiver gauge theory with only unitary gauge nodes.

arxiv-2406-12318.title: Intrinsic phenomena of delta shock waves in a more realistic Chaplygin Aw-Rascle model
arxiv-2406-12318.creator: Priyanka, M. Zafar
arxiv-2406-12318.description: Abstract . The motivation of this study is to find the Riemann solutions of Aw-Rascle model with a more realistic version of extended Chaplygin gas. Firstly, we establish the Riemann solutions with two different structures, viz., a shock wave followed by the contact discontinuity and a rarefaction wave followed by the contact discontinuity.

arxiv-2412-04365.title: Homological smoothness of Hopf-Galois extensions
arxiv-2412-04365.creator: Julian Le Clainche
arxiv-2412-04365.description: Abstract We show that if H H is a Hopf algebra with bijective antipode and B ⊂ A B\subset A is a faithfully flat H H -Galois extension, then A A is homologically smooth if H H and B B are.

arxiv-2505-13346.title: J4R: Learning to Judge with Equivalent Initial State Group Relative Policy Optimization
arxiv-2505-13346.creator: Austin Xu, Yilun Zhou, Xuan-Phi Nguyen, Caiming Xiong, Shafiq Joty
arxiv-2505-13346.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Austin Xu, Yilun Zhou, Xuan-Phi Nguyen, Caiming Xiong, Shafiq Joty. To keep pace with the increasing pace of large language models (LLM) development, model output evaluation has transitioned away from time-consuming human evaluation to automatic evaluation, where LLMs themselves are tasked with assessing and critiquing other model outputs. LLM-as-judge models are a class of generative evaluators that excel in evaluating relatively simple domains, like chat quality, but struggle in reasoning intensive domains where model responses contain more substantive and challenging content.

arxiv-2506-20880.title: Global properties and stability of transonic plasma acceleration in the magnetic nozzle
arxiv-2506-20880.creator: N. Sheth, A. Smolyakov, J. Deguire, S. Pande, P.N. Yushmanov
arxiv-2506-20880.description: Abstract It is shown that transonic plasma acceleration in the converging-diverging magnetic field (magnetic nozzle) follows the unique global solution which is fully defined by the magnetic field. Such solution, which was analytically obtained earlier in the paraxial approximation, is compared here with results of the axisymmetric two-dimensional ( r − z r-z ) magnetohydrodynamics(MHD) simulations.

pmc-10628265.title: Three-Dimensional Printing of Models of Patellofemoral Joint Articular Cartilage in Patients With Patella Instability for Observing Joint Congruity
pmc-10628265.creator: Brian G Beitler, Kunsel Kunsel, Kristin E Yu, Annie Wang, Steven M Tommasini, Daniel H Wiznia, John P Fulkerson
pmc-10628265.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Three-dimensional (3D) modeling and printing are increasingly used in the field of orthopaedic surgery for both research and patient care. One area where they are particularly helpful is in improving our understanding of the patellofemoral (PF) joint. Heretofore, morphological studies that use 3D models of the PF joint have primarily been based on computed tomography imaging data and thus do not incorporate articular cartilage.

pmc-10671869.title: Astrocytes: Lessons Learned from the Cuprizone Model
pmc-10671869.creator: Markus Kipp, Fabio Cavaliere
pmc-10671869.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). A diverse array of neurological and psychiatric disorders, including multiple sclerosis, Alzheimer’s disease, and schizophrenia, exhibit distinct myelin abnormalities at both the molecular and histological levels. These aberrations are closely linked to dysfunction of oligodendrocytes and alterations in myelin structure, which may be pivotal factors contributing to the disconnection of brain regions and the resulting characteristic clinical impairments observed in these conditions.

pmc-10694415.title: Classification and prediction of the effects of nutritional intake on diabetes mellitus using artificial neural network sensitivity analysis: 7th Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
pmc-10694415.creator: Kyungjin Chang, Songmin Yoo, Simyeol Lee
pmc-10694415.description: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVESThis study aimed to predict the association between nutritional intake and diabetes mellitus (DM) by developing an artificial neural network (ANN) model for older adults.SUBJECTS/METHODSParticipants aged over 65 years from the 7th (2016–2018) Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey were included.

pmc-11464507.title: Complex transcriptional regulations of a hyperparasitic quadripartite system in giant viruses infecting protists
pmc-11464507.creator: Alexandra Bessenay, Hugo Bisio, Lucid Belmudes, Yohann Couté, Lionel Bertaux, Jean-Michel Claverie, Chantal Abergel, Sandra Jeudy, Matthieu Legendre
pmc-11464507.description: Hyperparasitism is a common pattern in nature that is not limited to cellular organisms. Giant viruses infecting protists can be hyperparasitized by smaller ones named virophages. In addition, both may carry episomal DNA molecules known as transpovirons in their particles.

pmc-12613625.title: The stroke that unveiled a silent threat: rupture and thrombosis of hydatid cyst in the left ventricle- a case report
pmc-12613625.creator: Ounci Es-Saad, Ayoub Abetti, Hajar Belghit, Abdellahi Darraz, Rajae Alkouh, Smael Labib
pmc-12613625.description: BackgroundCardiac hydatid cysts are rare, even in endemic regions, and are typically asymptomatic. Systemic embolism resulting from rupture of a cardiac hydatid cyst is exceptionally uncommon, and thrombosis within a cyst has not previously been reported.Case presentationWe describe the case of a 7-year-old girl who presented with left hemiplegia and aphasia secondary to an ischemic stroke.

pmc-12741085.title: A window of opportunity: a pilot study exploring smoking cessation support during COPD hospitalisation
pmc-12741085.creator: Ingeborg Farver-Vestergaard, Anders Løkke, Jannie Christina Frølund
pmc-12741085.description: BackgroundA significant proportion of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) continue smoking after diagnosis, contributing to increased symptom burden, more frequent exacerbations and poorer long-term outcomes. Hospitalisation due to COPD exacerbation may serve as a “window of opportunity” for delivering smoking cessation support.

pmc-13057024.title: Lightweight convolutional neural network for real-time earthquake P-wave detection on edge devices in New Zealand
pmc-13057024.creator: Danuka Ravishan, Raj Prasanna, Pasan Herath, Emma E. H. Doyle
pmc-13057024.description: Earthquake P-wave detection is the first and most critical step in Earthquake Early Warning (EEW), as detection speed determines how much time is available before strong shaking arrives, while detection accuracy governs the reliability of the warning. Conventional P-Wave detection methods such as Short-Term Average over Long-Term Average (STA/LTA) often struggle in complex noise environments and exhibit higher detection latency.

pmc-13339973.title: The Experiences of Family Dyads During the Gender Identity Transition Process of Children and Adolescents
pmc-13339973.creator: Augusto Krindges, Guilherme da Silva Biasus, Carolina Andrade Costa, Tania Christiane Ferreira Bispo, Anderson Reis de Sousa, Jeferson Santos Araújo
pmc-13339973.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to analyse the transition process experienced by mother/father dyads when they recognise their children's gender dysphoria.MethodologyThe study employed a qualitative approach, based on interpretative description and the theoretical support of the transitions theory, in which 10 dyads participated. The interviews were conducted using a semi‐structured script, recorded, transcribed, and subjected to reflective thematic analysis.

pmc-13402765.title: Persistent Food Insecurity and Overweight/Obesity Risk in Offspring of Individuals With Gestational Diabetes
pmc-13402765.creator: Keally Haushalter, Jaimie N Davis, Yeyi Zhu, Joan C Lo, Erin A Hudson, Alexis King, Louise Greenspan, Jami Josefson, Erica P Gunderson
pmc-13402765.description: ObjectiveAssess how changes in food insecurity in the first 2 years of life are associated with overweight and obesity among children 6–11 years old born to mothers with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).MethodsThis secondary analysis utilised data from the Study of Women, Infant Feeding and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus after GDM pregnancy, a prospective cohort of 1033 mother–child dyads.

pmc-13416070.title: Uncertainty-aware instance-wise feature selection with adaptive graph regularization
pmc-13416070.creator: G Kirubavathi, K J Vijayavarsini, G S Vruthula Shruthi
pmc-13416070.description: Instance-wise feature selection aims at discovering the most relevant set of attributes for each particular sample, providing a natural direction for achieving adaptive learning on inputs of heterogeneous and high-dimensional nature. While recent neural-net models made impressive advances, all current methods share a common drawback: the selected feature mask is considered as a definite one.

pmc-13669287.title: Targeting P2Y14R inhibits proliferation of cervical cancer cells and organoids and activates cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling pathway
pmc-13669287.creator: Rui Li, Hai-Yun Xiong, Shi-Yu Chen, Yong Tang, Wen-Bin Ma
pmc-13669287.description: Purinergic signaling has been widely recognized as a critical regulator of tumor progression, yet the role of P2Y14R in cervical cancer remains unclear. This study used the P2Y14R antagonist PPTN in in vitro cell experiments; the results showed that it significantly inhibited cell proliferation and increased LDH release.
